You are acting as a rigorous research copilot for a Master’s level machine learning project in financial time series. I am designing a research project on a multi horizon multimodal model for event driven financial forecasting. Important framing: * This is not a pure price prediction project. * This is not a trading bot. * The research focus is temporal representation learning, multimodal fusion, multi task prediction, and decision scoring under uncertainty. * The central hypothesis is that an aggregated temporal event state built from recent news can improve multi horizon prediction over market only baselines. * The project should avoid assuming that individual news effects can be cleanly isolated, because financial news overlaps continuously. I want you to help me design the project at research quality and with strict honesty. Do not invent datasets, papers, metrics, or results. If something is uncertain, say so explicitly. 4) Stooq (market data EOD, mas “liviano”, pero ojo)

JSON

Dijiste:

Can i normalize splits in a way that the stock price is continuos from that start as if it was already splitted from the start

ChatGPT dijo:

Yes. What you want is the standard split adjustment (back adjustment): rescale all past prices so the series is continuous, as if today’s share count had always existed since the start date.

A stock split does not change market value, it only changes the unit scale (shares) so the raw price series jumps mechanically. Split adjustment removes that mechanical jump.

The idea in one line

If there is a split with factor s=new sharesold sharess = \frac{\text{new shares}}{\text{old shares}}s=old sharesnew shares​:

  • Prices before the split should be divided by sss

  • Volumes before the split should be multiplied by sss

Example: 2 for 1 split, s=2s = 2s=2. A pre split close of 100 becomes 50 after adjustment, and a pre split volume of 1M becomes 2M.

With multiple splits, you apply the cumulative product of all later splits.

Method A (best if you have explicit split factors)

Assume you have daily data with at least:

  • open, high, low, close, volume

  • and a split_factor per day, where:

    • split_factor = 1 on normal days

    • split_factor = s on the split effective date, with s=newolds = \frac{\text{new}}{\text{old}}s=oldnew​

    • reverse splits will have s<1s < 1s<1

Math

Let dates be in increasing order. Define:

Ct=∏τ>tsτC_t = \prod_{\tau > t} s_\tauCt​=τ>t∏​sτ​

That is, CtC_tCt​ is the product of split factors that occur after day ttt.

Then:

price_adjt=pricetCt,volume_adjt=volumet⋅Ct\text{price\_adj}_t = \frac{\text{price}_t}{C_t}, \quad \text{volume\_adj}_t = \text{volume}_t \cdot C_tprice_adjt​=Ct​pricet​​,volume_adjt​=volumet​⋅Ct​

Apply that to open, high, low, close.

Pandas implementation

Python
import pandas as pd

def adjust_for_splits(df: pd.DataFrame,
                      price_cols=("open", "high", "low", "close"),
                      volume_col="volume",
                      split_col="split_factor") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Back adjust prices so the series is continuous across splits.
    Assumes split_factor = new_shares / old_shares on the split effective date.
    """
    out = df.sort_values("date").copy()

    if split_col not in out.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing {split_col}. Provide split factors or use Method B.")

    # Ensure split_factor exists for every row
    out[split_col] = out[split_col].fillna(1.0).astype(float)

    # Product of splits after each date:
    # cumprod gives product up to t, so we shift to get "after t"
    cum_to_t = out[split_col].cumprod()
    total = cum_to_t.iloc[-1]
    C_after_t = (total / cum_to_t).astype(float)  # product of splits after t

    for c in price_cols:
        out[c + "_adj"] = out[c].astype(float) / C_after_t

    if volume_col in out.columns:
        out[volume_col + "_adj"] = out[volume_col].astype(float) * C_after_t

    return out

Sanity checks you should run

For each row:

  • high_adj >= max(open_adj, close_adj)

  • low_adj <= min(open_adj, close_adj)

  • Around a split date, the adjusted close should not jump by the split ratio (it can still move due to real returns)

Also verify your provider’s meaning of split_factor:

  • Some APIs store the inverse ratio. If you are unsure, inspect one known split date and see whether raw close roughly scales by sss across the split. If it does the opposite, invert the factor.

Method B (if you only have adjusted close but no explicit split factor)

Many providers expose both close and adj_close. Often adj_close is already adjusted for splits, sometimes also for dividends.

You can compute a daily adjustment ratio:

rt=adj_closetclosetr_t = \frac{\text{adj\_close}_t}{\text{close}_t}rt​=closet​adj_closet​​

Then:

  • open_adj = open * r

  • high_adj = high * r

  • low_adj = low * r

  • close_adj = close * r (will match adj_close)

  • volume_adj = volume / r (inverse scaling, because price scaling is inverse of share scaling)

Code:

Python
def adjust_using_adj_close(df: pd.DataFrame,
                           price_cols=("open", "high", "low", "close"),
                           close_col="close",
                           adj_close_col="adj_close",
                           volume_col="volume") -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = df.sort_values("date").copy()

    r = out[adj_close_col].astype(float) / out[close_col].astype(float)

    for c in price_cols:
        out[c + "_adj"] = out[c].astype(float) * r

    if volume_col in out.columns:
        out[volume_col + "_adj"] = out[volume_col].astype(float) / r

    return out

Important caveat:

  • If adj_close includes dividends, then this method creates a “total return style” adjustment, not just split adjustment. That may be good, but you must state it clearly in your thesis.

What this achieves (and what it does not)

Achieves

  • A continuous price history “as if” today’s share count applied from the beginning

  • Clean forward return labels that are not polluted by split jumps

Does not achieve

  • It does not remove true economic discontinuities like large overnight gaps due to real news

  • It does not automatically account for dividends, spin offs, mergers unless your adjusted series includes them and you choose to use it

If you tell me which data source you are using for OHLC (Finnhub, Alpha Vantage, Tiingo, Polygon, etc.), I can map this to their exact fields and point out the one place where people commonly invert the split factor.

6) Event state module (the heart of your project)

You want an “evolving event state” that does not assume isolated effects.

Minimal, strong baseline (fast + defensible)

For each stock-day, aggregate embeddings in the lookback window with time decay:

wn=exp⁡(−λΔn)w_n = \exp(-\lambda \Delta_n)wn​=exp(−λΔn​) si,t=∑n∈Ni,twnen∑n∈Ni,twn+ϵs_{i,t} = \frac{\sum_{n \in \mathcal{N}_{i,t}} w_n e_n}{\sum_{n \in \mathcal{N}_{i,t}} w_n + \epsilon}si,t​=∑n∈Ni,t​​wn​+ϵ∑n∈Ni,t​​wn​en​​

Then concatenate auxiliary scalars:

  • burstiness (count / avg count last K days)

  • recency stats (min age, mean age)

  • novelty proxy (cosine distance between current state and previous day state)

  • optional conflict proxy (dispersion: average pairwise cosine distance among embeddings)

This gives you a robust “event state” without a heavy transformer.

Optional upgrade (still feasible)

A tiny attention pooling layer:

This lets the model pick “dominant narrative” items.

Stage 1: classical baselines (sanity + thesis credibility)

Stage 2: market-only multi-horizon neural baseline

  • Input: market features over last WWW days (e.g. 20)

  • Model: MLP on engineered features (simplest) or 1D temporal conv (still manageable)

  • Output: multi-head for horizons

Stage 3: multimodal main model (recommended)

Recommended for Master scope: “EventState pooling + Fusion MLP + Multi-head outputs”

  • Market encoder: small MLP (or temporal conv if using sequences)

  • News encoder: precomputed embeddings + pooling/attention → event state vector

  • Fusion: concatenate + gating (FiLM or sigmoid gate)

  • Heads: horizon-specific output heads

This is implementable, interpretable, and fast.

8) Loss design (practical + “risk-aware”)

If you want “risk-adjusted outcomes under uncertainty” without overengineering:

Must do

  • predict forward excess returns (or market-neutral returns) per horizon with Huber loss

  • predict direction (up/down) with BCE loss

  • total loss = weighted sum over horizons and tasks

Strongly recommended (uncertainty)

Add heteroscedastic regression per horizon:

  • output (μ,log⁡σ)(\mu, \log\sigma)(μ,logσ)

  • use Gaussian NLL (with clipping on log sigma)

This lets you build calibrated confidence intervals and decision scores.

Optional

Quantile regression (pinball loss) at 0.1/0.5/0.9.

Splits

Use walk-forward, e.g.:

  • Train: 2016–2021

  • Val: 2022

  • Test: 2023
    Then roll forward.

Overlapping horizons: embargo / purge gap

If you label with 20-day forward returns and your val starts on Jan 1, you should embargo the last 20 trading days of train before val to avoid information bleed via overlapping targets.

You must implement this explicitly.

EOD cutoff rule

For each trading day ttt:

  • define cutoff timestamp CtC_tCt​ = market close time for that day

  • include only news with published_ts <= C_t

  • the label uses price at t+ht+ht+h and price at ttt (close-to-close)

You must define timezone conversion and holidays.

10) Code skeletons (what I’d actually write)

10.1 Event state pooling (PyTorch module)

Python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class DecayPooling(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, emb_dim: int, add_stats: bool = True):
        super().__init__()
        self.emb_dim = emb_dim
        self.add_stats = add_stats

    def forward(self, E, ages, mask, lam):
        """
        E: (B, N, D) embeddings
        ages: (B, N) age in days (float)
        mask: (B, N) 1 if valid news else 0
        lam: scalar or (B, 1) decay strength
        """
        # weights: exp(-lam * age)
        w = torch.exp(-lam * ages) * mask
        w_sum = w.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-6)
        s = (E * w.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=1) / w_sum  # (B, D)

        if not self.add_stats:
            return s

        # simple auxiliary stats (all cheap and useful)
        count = mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        mean_age = (ages * mask).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) / count.clamp_min(1.0)
        min_age = ages.masked_fill(mask == 0, 1e9).min(dim=1).values.unsqueeze(-1)
        stats = torch.cat([count, mean_age, min_age], dim=1)  # (B, 3)
        return torch.cat([s, stats], dim=1)

You will tailor:

  • what stats you include

  • whether lam is global, learned, or horizon-dependent

10.2 Fusion + multi-horizon heads

Python
class MultiHorizonModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, mkt_dim, evt_dim, hidden=256, horizons=(1,5,20), predict_sigma=True):
        super().__init__()
        self.horizons = horizons
        self.predict_sigma = predict_sigma

        self.mkt_enc = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(mkt_dim, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
            nn.Linear(hidden, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
        )

        self.fuse = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden + evt_dim, hidden),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.1),
        )

        out_dim_per_h = 2 if predict_sigma else 1
        self.ret_heads = nn.ModuleDict({
            str(h): nn.Linear(hidden, out_dim_per_h) for h in horizons
        })
        self.dir_heads = nn.ModuleDict({
            str(h): nn.Linear(hidden, 1) for h in horizons
        })

    def forward(self, x_mkt, s_evt):
        hm = self.mkt_enc(x_mkt)
        z = self.fuse(torch.cat([hm, s_evt], dim=1))

        out = {}
        for h in self.horizons:
            r = self.ret_heads[str(h)](z)
            d = self.dir_heads[str(h)](z)
            out[h] = {"ret": r, "dir_logit": d}
        return out

You will tailor:

  • which tasks you predict (ret only vs ret+dir+downside)

  • loss weights per horizon

Skeleton:

Python
import os, json, time
import requests
import pandas as pd

ALPHAVANTAGE_URL = "https://www.alphavantage.co/query"

def fetch_av_daily_adjusted(symbol: str, api_key: str, outputsize: str = "full") -> dict:
    params = {
        "function": "TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED",
        "symbol": symbol,
        "outputsize": outputsize,
        "datatype": "json",
        "apikey": api_key,
    }
    r = requests.get(ALPHAVANTAGE_URL, params=params, timeout=60)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

def av_json_to_df(symbol: str, payload: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ts = payload.get("Time Series (Daily)")
    if ts is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing Time Series (Daily) for {symbol}. Keys: {list(payload.keys())[:10]}")
    rows = []
    for date_str, v in ts.items():
        rows.append({
            "date": date_str,
            "ticker": symbol,
            "open": float(v["1. open"]),
            "high": float(v["2. high"]),
            "low": float(v["3. low"]),
            "close": float(v["4. close"]),
            "adj_close": float(v["5. adjusted close"]),
            "volume": float(v["6. volume"]),
            "dividend": float(v["7. dividend amount"]),
            "split_coef": float(v["8. split coefficient"]),
        })
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    return df.sort_values(["ticker", "date"]).reset_index(drop=True)

Skeleton:

Python
import finnhub
import pandas as pd

def fetch_finnhub_company_news(client: finnhub.Client, symbol: str, start: str, end: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    items = client.company_news(symbol, _from=start, to=end)
    df = pd.DataFrame(items)
    if not df.empty:
        df["ticker"] = symbol
        df["published_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(df["datetime"], unit="s", utc=True)
    return df

Why this structure works

1) Clean separation of concerns

  • data/raw is immutable inputs (API dumps). You never “fix” raw data, you reprocess into interim or final.

  • src/ contains all logic. No logic lives in notebooks.

  • runs/ contains per experiment outputs so you can reproduce and compare.

2) It supports the right workflow for your sources

Alpha Vantage rate limits force a staged pipeline:

  • Download once, cache forever in data/raw/alphavantage

  • Process into parquet once

  • Train and iterate without touching the APIs again

3) It makes leakage harder to accidentally introduce

You can put all time cutoff logic in one place:

  • src/data/align_eod_cutoff.py
    and unit test it in:

  • tests/test_leakage.py

Naming conventions that will save you later

Data file rules

  • Raw files are chunked and named deterministically, for example:

    • data/raw/alphavantage/AAPL_TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED.json

    • data/raw/finnhub/AAPL_news_2024-01-01_2024-03-31.json

  • Processed parquet tables are stable and versioned by rebuild, not by hand edits.

IDs and keys

Use consistent keys everywhere:

  • ticker as uppercase string

  • date as trading date (no timezone)

  • published_ts as UTC timestamp

  • article_id as a stable hash if the provider does not guarantee a unique id, for example hash of url + published_ts + source

Must do, strongly recommended, optional

Must do

  • .env.example and load secrets from .env (never commit API keys)

  • data/raw, data/interim, data/final separation

  • runs/ per experiment with resolved config saved

  • tests/ at least for leakage and label alignment

Strongly recommended

  • configs/ with one source of truth for horizons, lookback, cutoffs, split strategy

  • A Makefile with commands like:

    • make data

    • make embeddings

    • make train

    • make eval

  • Store final modeling tables in parquet for speed and schema consistency

Optional extensions

  • DVC for data versioning if your raw dumps and embeddings are large

  • MLflow or W and B for tracking, if runs/ becomes hard to manage

  • Docker or Apptainer if you need environment portability across machines

What you will tailor

  • Your exact dataset build steps inside src/cli/build_dataset.py

  • Your split policy in src/split/walk_forward.py and src/split/embargo.py

  • Your event state implementation in src/features/event_state.py

If you tell me whether you want to use Hydra for configs or keep it simple with argparse + YAML, I can adapt this into a minimal “starter skeleton” with exact filenames and the CLI commands you’ll run on Linux.

Por que Keys.py es mala idea en la practica

1) Riesgo real de commiteo accidental

Aunque lo tengas en .gitignore, pasa mucho:

  • lo copias, lo renombras, o alguien te lo pide

  • haces git add -A sin revisar

  • terminas rotando keys a mitad del proyecto

2) Reproducibilidad y portabilidad

Cuando corras en otra maquina, VM, o cluster:

  • tienes que recrear el archivo manualmente

  • no queda estandarizado que variables existen

  • no es compatible con herramientas de CI o experiment runners

3) Seguridad y logs

A veces se imprime el objeto o se loguea el modulo sin querer. Con env vars, es mas facil evitarlo.

Mejor alternativa (simple): .env + .env.example

Estructura

  • .env (NO se commitea)

  • .env.example (SI se commitea, sin secretos)

Ejemplo .env.example:

Bash
FINNHUB_API_KEY=your_key_here
ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY=your_key_here

Carga en Python

Python
from dotenv import load_dotenv
import os

load_dotenv()  # loads .env

FINNHUB_API_KEY = os.environ["FINNHUB_API_KEY"]
ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY = os.environ["ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY"]

Ventajas:

  • funciona igual local, en github, en cluster

  • config mas estandar

  • mas dificil filtrar keys por accidente

  • y ahi decides si lee de env o de Keys

3) Asegura .gitignore

Incluye explicitamente:

scraping/Keys.py
.env

Recomendacion final (para tu proyecto)

Dado que vas a iterar mucho (dataset build, runs, etc.) y probablemente quieras compartir el repo con tu profe o subirlo a GitHub:

  • Pasa a .env + dotenv

Yes, this structure is absolutely “good enough” to build a thesis-grade pipeline. It’s already much closer to what you want (clean separation of src/, data/, configs/, runs/, tests/).

That said, I’d make a few targeted tweaks now to avoid future pain.

1) Folder structure feedback

What you did really well

  • src/ is organized by responsibility (data, features, models, split, utils). That scales.

  • configs/ exists. You’ll need it for ablations and walk-forward.

  • data/raw → interim → final is the correct mental model for your AlphaVantage rate limit workflow.

  • tests/ includes leakage and label tests. That’s exactly what makes this credible.

The 3 changes I strongly recommend

A) Don’t keep checkpoints in artifacts/checkpoints

You already have runs/. For reproducibility, it’s better if each run owns its own artifacts.

Recommended rule:

  • runs/<run_id>/checkpoints/ for run-specific models

  • artifacts/figures and artifacts/tables only for aggregated / publication-ready outputs

If you keep artifacts/checkpoints, you’ll eventually mix models from different configs or splits.

B) Add an explicit “universe snapshot” location

You will download S&P 500 tickers once, but the list changes. Store the snapshot you used:

  • data/raw/universe/sp500_YYYY-MM-DD.csv

This is essential to make your results reproducible.

C) Add .env.example and never store keys in code

Even if you don’t commit them, keys in code makes environments harder to manage. A .env workflow is cleaner.

2) Your plan: “download all S&P 500 tickers first”

Conceptually it’s fine, but with Alpha Vantage’s free tier you must plan around the constraint:

  • Alpha Vantage free usage limit is 25 requests per day. alphavantage.co

So 500 tickers will take at least 20 days just to fetch one endpoint per ticker, even before retries.

My suggestion: do it in two phases to save time

Phase 1 (get productive fast)

Pick a pilot set of ~30 tickers (diverse sectors) and build the full pipeline end to end:

  • raw downloads

  • parsing

  • split adjustment handling (via daily adjusted endpoint)

  • news ingestion

  • EOD cutoff filtering

  • embeddings

  • event state

  • training + evaluation

This prevents you from waiting 2–3 weeks before you can even start modeling.

Phase 2 (scale up safely)

Start collecting S&P500 OHLCV in the background incrementally (daily runs of your downloader). Your code should:

  • skip tickers already cached

  • write one raw json per ticker

  • keep a “download ledger” (csv or sqlite) of status per ticker

This fits the 25/day constraint without becoming a manual nightmare.

3) Where to get S&P 500 tickers without hallucinating

Reality check on licensing

The official constituent data from S&P Dow Jones is something they license (they explicitly talk about licensing “constituent data”). S&P Global
So for a public thesis repo, the safest approach is usually:

  • use a public list (like Wikipedia) and snapshot it with date

  • document that it’s a public snapshot, not the licensed official constituent feed

Practical source

Wikipedia maintains a table with the S&P 500 components (Symbol, Security, Sector, etc.). Wikipedia

Implementation detail:

  • parse it once with pandas.read_html

  • save it to data/raw/universe/sp500_YYYY-MM-DD.csv

  • from then on, your pipeline uses that file, not the live page

4) Important gotcha: ticker format normalization

S&P500 tickers include share classes like BRK.B, BF.B etc. Different APIs sometimes want different formats (BRK.B vs BRK-B). I can’t truthfully guarantee which exact format Alpha Vantage expects for every class ticker without testing your key in practice.

So you should add:

  • src/data/ticker_normalization.py

  • a small test that tries a few known class tickers and logs which format succeeds

  • a persisted mapping file: data/raw/universe/ticker_map.csv

This single piece will prevent you from silently missing data for a subset of companies.

5) Minimal Makefile targets that match your folder layout

I’d wire your repo so you can do:

  • make universe (snapshot tickers)

  • make download_prices (resumable, respects rate limit)

  • make download_news

  • make embeddings

  • make build_final

  • make train

  • make eval

That way the whole pipeline is one command per phase.

Bottom line

Your structure is solid. If you do only three things now:

  1. move checkpoints under runs/<run_id>/

  2. snapshot and version the S&P500 universe file

  3. implement ticker normalization and a download ledger

you’ll avoid 80 percent of the pain people hit in financial ML projects.

If you want, paste your current download_prices.py outline (even rough), and I’ll tell you exactly how to design the resumable 25-per-day scheduler + caching layout so you can safely build the full S&P500 database over time.

1) Store API keys in a .env (where and how)

Where

Create .env at the repo root, same level as pyproject.toml, Makefile, README.md.

Example:

event-state-forecasting/.env

What to put in it

.env (do not commit):

Bash
ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY=put_your_key_here
FINNHUB_API_KEY=put_your_key_here

.env.example (commit this):

Then in CLI entrypoints, call load_dotenv() once.

2) Makefile targets: make universe and make download_prices

Add/merge these targets into your Makefile:

Makefile
# Makefile

PYTHON := python3
DATE := $(shell date +%F)

UNIVERSE_DIR := data/raw/universe
AV_RAW_DIR := data/raw/alphavantage
AV_PARSED_DIR := data/interim/alphavantage_prices

.PHONY: universe download_prices dirs

dirs:
	mkdir -p $(UNIVERSE_DIR) $(AV_RAW_DIR) $(AV_PARSED_DIR)

universe: dirs
	$(PYTHON) -m src.data.build_universe \
		--out $(UNIVERSE_DIR)/sp500_$(DATE).csv \
		--also-latest $(UNIVERSE_DIR)/sp500_latest.csv

download_prices: dirs
	$(PYTHON) -m src.data.download_prices \
		--universe $(UNIVERSE_DIR)/sp500_latest.csv \
		--raw-dir $(AV_RAW_DIR) \
		--parsed-dir $(AV_PARSED_DIR) \
		--function TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED \
		--outputsize full \
		--datatype json \
		--max-requests-per-day 25 \
		--sleep-seconds 15

Notes:

  • --outputsize full requests maximum historical depth (docs say “20+ years” for daily adjusted). alphavantage.co

  • --max-requests-per-day 25 matches your plan and the free-tier limit. alphavantage.co

  • --sleep-seconds 15 is a safe default throttle. (I’m not asserting a per-minute limit here because your requirement was “no hallucination”; this is just a conservative throttle.)

3) Code for make universe

This pulls S&P 500 constituents from Wikipedia and snapshots it. Wikipedia’s page includes a components table with the Symbol column. Wikipedia

# src/data/build_universe.py
import argparse
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

WIKI_SP500_URL = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies"


def fetch_sp500_table() -> pd.DataFrame:
    tables = pd.read_html(WIKI_SP500_URL)
    # The first table is typically the components table, but we guard by column name.
    for t in tables:
        cols = [c.strip() for c in t.columns.astype(str).tolist()]
        if "Symbol" in cols and "Security" in cols:
            t = t.copy()
            t.columns = cols
            return t
    raise RuntimeError("Could not find S&P 500 table with columns Symbol and Security")


def build_universe_df() -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = fetch_sp500_table()
    df["Symbol"] = df["Symbol"].astype(str).str.strip()

    # Keep useful columns; if some are missing, keep what exists.
    keep = [c for c in ["Symbol", "Security", "GICS Sector", "GICS Sub-Industry",
                        "Headquarters Location", "Date added", "CIK", "Founded"]
            if c in df.columns]
    df = df[keep].copy()

    df = df.rename(columns={"Symbol": "ticker", "Security": "security"})
    df["snapshot_utc"] = datetime.utcnow().isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"
    df = df.sort_values("ticker").reset_index(drop=True)
    return df


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="Output CSV path for dated snapshot")
    ap.add_argument("--also-latest", default=None, help="Optional path to also write sp500_latest.csv")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out_path = Path(args.out)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    df = build_universe_df()
    df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)

    if args.also_latest:
        latest_path = Path(args.also_latest)
        latest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        df.to_csv(latest_path, index=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

This gives you a reproducible universe snapshot file you can cite and freeze per experiment.

# src/data/alphavantage_client.py
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

import requests
from dotenv import load_dotenv

ALPHAVANTAGE_URL = "https://www.alphavantage.co/query"


@dataclass
class AlphaVantageClient:
    api_key: str
    timeout_s: int = 60

    @staticmethod
    def from_env() -> "AlphaVantageClient":
        load_dotenv()
        key = os.getenv("ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY")
        if not key:
            raise RuntimeError("Missing ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY in environment (.env at repo root)")
        return AlphaVantageClient(api_key=key)

    def query(self, function: str, symbol: str, outputsize: str, datatype: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        params = {
            "function": function,
            "symbol": symbol,
            "outputsize": outputsize,
            "datatype": datatype,
            "apikey": self.api_key,
        }
        r = requests.get(ALPHAVANTAGE_URL, params=params, timeout=self.timeout_s)
        r.raise_for_status()
        if datatype.lower() == "csv":
            # Caller should handle CSV separately if needed.
            return {"_csv": r.text}
        return r.json()


def is_rate_limited(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    # Alpha Vantage often returns a JSON with a "Note" or "Information" key when throttled.
    keys = set(payload.keys())
    return ("Note" in keys) or ("Information" in keys)

src/data/download_prices.py

This script:

  • reads tickers from data/raw/universe/sp500_latest.csv

  • requests max history

  • writes raw JSON per ticker to data/raw/alphavantage/<ticker>.json

  • writes parsed parquet per ticker to data/interim/alphavantage_prices/<ticker>.parquet

  • maintains a ledger data/raw/alphavantage/download_ledger.csv for resume/debug

  • stops cleanly when it hits daily max requests or rate limit

# src/data/download_prices.py
import argparse
import json
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

import pandas as pd
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from src.data.alphavantage_client import AlphaVantageClient, is_rate_limited


DAILY_KEYS = [
    "1. open",
    "2. high",
    "3. low",
    "4. close",
    "5. adjusted close",
    "6. volume",
    "7. dividend amount",
    "8. split coefficient",
]


def _now_utc() -> str:
    return datetime.utcnow().isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"


def read_universe(universe_csv: Path) -> List[str]:
    df = pd.read_csv(universe_csv)
    if "ticker" not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("Universe file must have a 'ticker' column")
    tickers = df["ticker"].astype(str).str.strip().tolist()
    return [t for t in tickers if t]


def choose_symbol_variants(ticker: str) -> List[str]:
    # Some providers differ on class tickers like BRK.B vs BRK-B.
    # We do not assume which one AV accepts; we try a small set.
    variants = [ticker]
    if "." in ticker:
        variants.append(ticker.replace(".", "-"))
    if "-" in ticker:
        variants.append(ticker.replace("-", "."))
    # Deduplicate, keep order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for v in variants:
        if v not in seen:
            seen.add(v)
            out.append(v)
    return out


def parse_daily_adjusted_json(symbol_used: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ts = payload.get("Time Series (Daily)")
    if ts is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing 'Time Series (Daily)' in response for {symbol_used}. Keys={list(payload.keys())[:8]}")

    rows = []
    for date_str, v in ts.items():
        # Guard missing keys
        row = {
            "date": pd.to_datetime(date_str),
            "ticker": symbol_used,
        }
        for k in DAILY_KEYS:
            if k in v:
                col = k.split(". ", 1)[1].replace(" ", "_")  # "open", "adjusted_close", ...
                row[col] = float(v[k])
        rows.append(row)

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["ticker", "date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    return df


def append_ledger(ledger_path: Path, record: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    ledger_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    df = pd.DataFrame([record])
    if ledger_path.exists():
        df.to_csv(ledger_path, mode="a", header=False, index=False)
    else:
        df.to_csv(ledger_path, index=False)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--universe", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--raw-dir", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--parsed-dir", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--function", default="TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED")
    ap.add_argument("--outputsize", default="full", choices=["compact", "full"])
    ap.add_argument("--datatype", default="json", choices=["json", "csv"])
    ap.add_argument("--max-requests-per-day", type=int, default=25)
    ap.add_argument("--sleep-seconds", type=float, default=15.0)
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    load_dotenv()
    client = AlphaVantageClient.from_env()

    tickers = read_universe(args.universe)

    args.raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.parsed_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ledger_path = args.raw_dir / "download_ledger.csv"

    requests_used = 0

    for ticker in tickers:
        if requests_used >= args.max_requests_per_day:
            print(f"[STOP] Reached max requests per day: {args.max_requests_per_day}")
            break

        raw_path = args.raw_dir / f"{ticker}.json"
        parsed_path = args.parsed_dir / f"{ticker}.parquet"

        if not args.force and raw_path.exists() and parsed_path.exists():
            continue

        variants = choose_symbol_variants(ticker)
        success = False
        last_error = None
        used_symbol = None
        payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

        for sym in variants:
            try:
                payload = client.query(
                    function=args.function,
                    symbol=sym,
                    outputsize=args.outputsize,
                    datatype=args.datatype,
                )
                requests_used += 1
                used_symbol = sym

                if args.datatype == "csv":
                    # Save raw csv text for later parsing if you choose that mode
                    raw_path = args.raw_dir / f"{ticker}.csv"
                    raw_path.write_text(payload["_csv"], encoding="utf-8")
                    # You can add csv parsing later if needed
                    success = True
                    break

                # JSON mode
                if is_rate_limited(payload):
                    append_ledger(ledger_path, {
                        "ts_utc": _now_utc(),
                        "ticker": ticker,
                        "symbol_used": sym,
                        "function": args.function,
                        "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                        "status": "rate_limited",
                        "message": payload.get("Note") or payload.get("Information"),
                    })
                    print("[STOP] Rate limited response received from Alpha Vantage.")
                    return

                if "Error Message" in payload:
                    last_error = payload.get("Error Message")
                    append_ledger(ledger_path, {
                        "ts_utc": _now_utc(),
                        "ticker": ticker,
                        "symbol_used": sym,
                        "function": args.function,
                        "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                        "status": "error",
                        "message": last_error,
                    })
                    continue

                # Save raw JSON for traceability
                raw_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload), encoding="utf-8")

                # Parse to parquet per ticker
                df = parse_daily_adjusted_json(sym, payload)
                df.to_parquet(parsed_path, index=False)

                append_ledger(ledger_path, {
                    "ts_utc": _now_utc(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "ok",
                    "n_rows": len(df),
                })
                success = True
                break

            except Exception as e:
                last_error = repr(e)
                append_ledger(ledger_path, {
                    "ts_utc": _now_utc(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "exception",
                    "message": last_error,
                })
                continue
            finally:
                # Conservative throttle
                time.sleep(args.sleep_seconds)

        if not success:
            print(f"[WARN] Failed ticker={ticker}. Last error={last_error}")

    print(f"[DONE] Requests used today: {requests_used}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

5) How this satisfies “download as much as possible”

Per ticker per request:

  • TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED includes open/high/low/close/volume, adjusted close, and split/dividend events. alphavantage.co+1

  • outputsize=full requests the full-length series (docs describe 20+ years on daily adjusted pages). alphavantage.co

But: if your key does not have access to full/premium, the ledger will show that clearly and you will still keep whatever the API returned. alphavantage.co+1

I’ll answer your question directly:

  • Yes, my implementation approach is materially better for your concrete constraints (Alpha Vantage 25/day + Finnhub + thesis reproducibility), because it is designed to be resumable, auditable, and offline-first.

  • Some parts of your drafts should not be implemented as written.

Below is the detailed comparison, and what to keep vs discard.

1) “Make universe” snippet: what’s good vs what to change

What is good and worth keeping

  1. Reproducibility note

“Store universe definition for reproducibility”
This is essential. You should snapshot the universe file (date-stamped) and also keep “latest”.

  1. Coverage validation function idea
    validate_universe_coverage() is absolutely useful.

You should keep it, but implement it using the data you actually downloaded, not by calling APIs again.

What is risky / misleading in that snippet

  1. Filtering by market cap and liquidity requires an extra dataset
    Your function signature suggests:

  • market cap >= 10B

  • average daily volume >= 1M USD
    But neither Alpha Vantage nor Finnhub “guarantee” you can get reliable market cap and liquidity for all tickers without additional endpoints/datasets. If you implement it without a verified source, you’ll drift into shaky assumptions.

Recommendation

  • For now, define universe as “S&P500 snapshot” and do liquidity filtering using OHLCV you downloaded (e.g., median dollar volume over last 60 trading days), not market cap.

  • If you later add market cap, do it explicitly as a new dataset with a cited source.

  1. “Data availability >= 2 years” is not a universe step—it's a post-download filter
    You can’t know availability until you download at least one ticker.

Recommendation

  • Universe building should produce candidates.

  • Then coverage validation should prune.

Practical improvement to your universe module

Keep a minimal universe builder:

  • snapshot S&P500 tickers (+ metadata from the page)

  • optional: later filter using your own downloaded OHLCV coverage and liquidity

This is exactly consistent with thesis honesty.

2) alphavantage_client.py: what’s good vs what to change

What is good and worth keeping

  • Having a dedicated client class is fine.

  • Retry + caching + error handling is good design.

Two key issues

  1. Your docstring says: “5 calls/min free tier”
    You asked me to avoid hallucinating. I’m not going to assert that as a fact here.

What we can cite confidently is:

  • 25 requests per day free tier limit. (alphavantage.co)

There are other limits, but unless you cite an official line you’ve verified, don’t bake “5/min” as a hard-coded rule. Use a conservative sleep and handle “Note/Information” responses.

  1. “fetch_batch” is the wrong abstraction under 25/day
    A “batch” implies you’ll fetch a list quickly. But with 25/day you want:

  • resumable loop

  • ledger

  • stop when daily quota reached

  • ability to run tomorrow and continue where you left off

So, instead of fetch_batch(symbols) -> dict, you want something like:

  • download_prices(universe_file), writing per-ticker artifacts and ledger.

3) download_prices.py: what’s good vs what to change

What is good and worth keeping

  • The integrity checks list is correct and important:

    • duplicates per ticker

    • OHLC logical consistency

    • no negative volume

    • no future dates
      These should become real tests and data validations.

  • Saving raw response + parsed table is correct.

What is missing (and why my approach is better)

  1. Ledger / resume
    Your plan does not explicitly include a persistent ledger. With Alpha Vantage you need it, otherwise you’ll waste daily requests repeating failures.

  2. Symbol variants
    S&P 500 includes share classes with periods in tickers. Different vendors treat them differently. Your draft doesn’t mention that.

My approach tries limited symbol variants and logs which one succeeded.

  1. Clear stop conditions
    When Alpha Vantage throttles, it often returns a JSON with keys like "Note" or "Information". You must stop and persist state. Your draft mentions “handle rate limit errors” but not the exact mechanism.

  2. Don’t return a combined DataFrame as the primary artifact
    For 500 tickers, returning a combined DF encourages “big in-memory pipeline” and makes crashes expensive.

Better pattern:

  • write per-ticker parquet

  • then separate “build_panel.py” merges into final panel parquet

That’s more robust and reproducible.

# src/data/build_universe.py
import argparse
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

WIKI_SP500_URL = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies"


def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.utcnow().isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"


def fetch_sp500_table() -> pd.DataFrame:
    tables = pd.read_html(WIKI_SP500_URL)
    for t in tables:
        cols = [str(c).strip() for c in t.columns.tolist()]
        if "Symbol" in cols and "Security" in cols:
            t = t.copy()
            t.columns = cols
            return t
    raise RuntimeError("Could not find S&P 500 table with columns Symbol and Security")


def build_universe_df() -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = fetch_sp500_table()

    df["Symbol"] = df["Symbol"].astype(str).str.strip()

    keep_cols = [
        "Symbol",
        "Security",
        "GICS Sector",
        "GICS Sub-Industry",
        "Headquarters Location",
        "Date added",
        "CIK",
        "Founded",
    ]
    keep_cols = [c for c in keep_cols if c in df.columns]
    df = df[keep_cols].copy()

    df = df.rename(columns={"Symbol": "ticker", "Security": "security"})
    df["snapshot_utc"] = _utc_now_iso()

    df = df.sort_values("ticker").reset_index(drop=True)
    return df


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--out",
        required=True,
        help="Output CSV path for dated snapshot, e.g. data/raw/universe/sp500_YYYY-MM-DD.csv",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--also-latest",
        default=None,
        help="Optional path to also write a rolling latest file, e.g. data/raw/universe/sp500_latest.csv",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out_path = Path(args.out)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    df = build_universe_df()
    df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)

    if args.also_latest:
        latest_path = Path(args.also_latest)
        latest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        df.to_csv(latest_path, index=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# src/data/alphavantage_client.py
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

import requests
from dotenv import find_dotenv, load_dotenv

ALPHAVANTAGE_URL = "https://www.alphavantage.co/query"


def is_rate_limited(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    # Alpha Vantage commonly uses these keys for throttling / premium messages
    return ("Note" in payload) or ("Information" in payload)


def extract_error(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    if "Error Message" in payload:
        return str(payload.get("Error Message"))
    if "Note" in payload:
        return str(payload.get("Note"))
    if "Information" in payload:
        return str(payload.get("Information"))
    if "message" in payload and isinstance(payload["message"], str):
        return payload["message"]
    return None


@dataclass
class AlphaVantageClient:
    api_key: str
    base_url: str = ALPHAVANTAGE_URL
    timeout_s: int = 60
    max_retries: int = 3
    retry_delay_s: float = 1.5

    @staticmethod
    def from_env() -> "AlphaVantageClient":
        # Loads .env from repo root if present
        load_dotenv(find_dotenv(usecwd=True))
        key = os.getenv("ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY")
        if not key:
            raise RuntimeError("Missing ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY in environment (.env at repo root)")
        return AlphaVantageClient(api_key=key)

    def query(
        self,
        function: str,
        symbol: str,
        outputsize: str = "full",
        datatype: str = "json",
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        params = {
            "function": function,
            "symbol": symbol,
            "outputsize": outputsize,
            "datatype": datatype,
            "apikey": self.api_key,
        }

        last_exc: Optional[Exception] = None
        for attempt in range(1, self.max_retries + 1):
            try:
                resp = requests.get(self.base_url, params=params, timeout=self.timeout_s)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                if datatype.lower() == "csv":
                    return {"_csv": resp.text}
                return resp.json()
            except Exception as e:
                last_exc = e
                if attempt < self.max_retries:
                    time.sleep(self.retry_delay_s * attempt)
                else:
                    raise RuntimeError(f"Alpha Vantage request failed after retries: {e}") from e

        # Unreachable, but keeps mypy happy
        raise RuntimeError(f"Alpha Vantage request failed: {last_exc}")

    def fetch_daily_adjusted(self, symbol: str, outputsize: str = "full") -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return self.query(
            function="TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED",
            symbol=symbol,
            outputsize=outputsize,
            datatype="json",
        )

src/data/download_prices.py

Python
# src/data/download_prices.py
import argparse
import json
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

import pandas as pd

from src.data.alphavantage_client import AlphaVantageClient, extract_error, is_rate_limited


DAILY_KEYS = [
    ("1. open", "open"),
    ("2. high", "high"),
    ("3. low", "low"),
    ("4. close", "close"),
    ("5. adjusted close", "adjusted_close"),
    ("6. volume", "volume"),
    ("7. dividend amount", "dividend_amount"),
    ("8. split coefficient", "split_coefficient"),
]


def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.utcnow().isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"


def read_universe(universe_csv: Path) -> List[str]:
    df = pd.read_csv(universe_csv)
    if "ticker" not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("Universe CSV must have a 'ticker' column")
    tickers = df["ticker"].astype(str).str.strip().tolist()
    tickers = [t for t in tickers if t]
    return tickers


def choose_symbol_variants(ticker: str) -> List[str]:
    # Some vendors use BRK.B while others require BRK-B (and vice versa).
    variants = [ticker]
    if "." in ticker:
        variants.append(ticker.replace(".", "-"))
    if "-" in ticker:
        variants.append(ticker.replace("-", "."))
    # Deduplicate preserve order
    out: List[str] = []
    seen = set()
    for v in variants:
        if v not in seen:
            seen.add(v)
            out.append(v)
    return out


def save_raw_json(path: Path, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=True), encoding="utf-8")


def parse_daily_adjusted_json(symbol_used: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ts = payload.get("Time Series (Daily)")
    if ts is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing 'Time Series (Daily)' for {symbol_used}. Keys={list(payload.keys())[:10]}")

    rows = []
    for date_str, v in ts.items():
        row: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "date": pd.to_datetime(date_str),
            "ticker": symbol_used,
        }
        for k, col in DAILY_KEYS:
            if k in v:
                row[col] = float(v[k])
        rows.append(row)

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["ticker", "date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    return df


def validate_price_data(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    # Basic integrity checks
    required = {"date", "ticker", "open", "high", "low", "close", "volume"}
    missing = required.difference(df.columns)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {sorted(missing)}")

    # No duplicates
    dup = df.duplicated(subset=["ticker", "date"]).any()
    if dup:
        raise ValueError("Duplicate (ticker, date) rows found")

    # No negative volume
    if (df["volume"] < 0).any():
        raise ValueError("Negative volume found")

    # OHLC consistency
    if (df["high"] < df[["open", "close"]].max(axis=1)).any():
        raise ValueError("Found high < max(open, close)")

    if (df["low"] > df[["open", "close"]].min(axis=1)).any():
        raise ValueError("Found low > min(open, close)")

    # No future dates (using local clock in UTC)
    today = pd.Timestamp.utcnow().normalize()
    if (df["date"] > today).any():
        raise ValueError("Found dates in the future")


def append_ledger(ledger_path: Path, record: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    ledger_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    row = pd.DataFrame([record])
    if ledger_path.exists():
        row.to_csv(ledger_path, mode="a", header=False, index=False)
    else:
        row.to_csv(ledger_path, index=False)


def download_one_symbol(
    client: AlphaVantageClient,
    ticker: str,
    function: str,
    outputsize: str,
) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[Dict[str, Any]], Optional[str]]:
    # Returns (symbol_used, payload, error_message)
    variants = choose_symbol_variants(ticker)
    last_err: Optional[str] = None

    for sym in variants:
        payload = client.query(function=function, symbol=sym, outputsize=outputsize, datatype="json")

        if is_rate_limited(payload):
            return sym, payload, "rate_limited"

        err = extract_error(payload)
        if err:
            last_err = err
            continue

        if "Time Series (Daily)" not in payload:
            last_err = f"missing_time_series_keys={list(payload.keys())[:10]}"
            continue

        return sym, payload, None

    return None, None, last_err or "unknown_error"


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--universe", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--raw-dir", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--parsed-dir", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--function", default="TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED")
    ap.add_argument("--outputsize", default="full", choices=["compact", "full"])
    ap.add_argument("--max-requests-per-day", type=int, default=25)
    ap.add_argument("--sleep-seconds", type=float, default=15.0)
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--start-date", default=None, help="Optional filter YYYY-MM-DD after parsing")
    ap.add_argument("--end-date", default=None, help="Optional filter YYYY-MM-DD after parsing")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    client = AlphaVantageClient.from_env()
    tickers = read_universe(args.universe)

    args.raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.parsed_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    ledger_path = args.raw_dir / "download_ledger.csv"

    requests_used = 0
    start_dt = pd.to_datetime(args.start_date) if args.start_date else None
    end_dt = pd.to_datetime(args.end_date) if args.end_date else None

    for ticker in tickers:
        if requests_used >= args.max_requests_per_day:
            print(f"[STOP] max_requests_per_day reached: {args.max_requests_per_day}")
            break

        raw_path = args.raw_dir / f"{ticker}.json"
        parsed_path = args.parsed_dir / f"{ticker}.parquet"

        if (not args.force) and raw_path.exists() and parsed_path.exists():
            continue

        # One API call per ticker attempt. We still count it even if ticker format fails.
        sym_used, payload, err = download_one_symbol(
            client=client,
            ticker=ticker,
            function=args.function,
            outputsize=args.outputsize,
        )
        requests_used += 1

        if err == "rate_limited":
            append_ledger(
                ledger_path,
                {
                    "ts_utc": _utc_now_iso(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym_used,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "rate_limited",
                    "message": extract_error(payload or {}) or "rate_limited",
                },
            )
            print("[STOP] rate limited response received, stopping for today")
            break

        if payload is None or sym_used is None:
            append_ledger(
                ledger_path,
                {
                    "ts_utc": _utc_now_iso(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym_used,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "error",
                    "message": err,
                },
            )
            print(f"[WARN] failed ticker={ticker} err={err}")
            time.sleep(args.sleep_seconds)
            continue

        # Save raw
        save_raw_json(raw_path, payload)

        # Parse and optionally filter
        try:
            df = parse_daily_adjusted_json(sym_used, payload)

            if start_dt is not None:
                df = df[df["date"] >= start_dt]
            if end_dt is not None:
                df = df[df["date"] <= end_dt]

            validate_price_data(df)

            df.to_parquet(parsed_path, index=False)

            append_ledger(
                ledger_path,
                {
                    "ts_utc": _utc_now_iso(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym_used,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "ok",
                    "n_rows": int(len(df)),
                },
            )
            print(f"[OK] {ticker} -> {sym_used} rows={len(df)}")
        except Exception as e:
            append_ledger(
                ledger_path,
                {
                    "ts_utc": _utc_now_iso(),
                    "ticker": ticker,
                    "symbol_used": sym_used,
                    "function": args.function,
                    "outputsize": args.outputsize,
                    "status": "parse_error",
                    "message": repr(e),
                },
            )
            print(f"[WARN] parse/validate failed ticker={ticker} err={e}")

        time.sleep(args.sleep_seconds)

    print(f"[DONE] requests_used={requests_used}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

If you want the next step after this: I can give you a src/cli/build_dataset.py that merges all per-ticker parquets into a single data/final/panel.parquet (plus a coverage report), but you asked for only these three files, so I’m stopping here.

Got it. The venv name/location (~/venv/ai) is not something you encode in pyproject.toml; that lives in your shell workflow. What does need to be correct in pyproject.toml is:

  1. core deps needed right now for make universe + make download_prices

  2. packaging config so src.* subpackages are included when you pip install .

  3. keep “future” deps, but move them to optional extras (or comment them)

Below is an edited version of your pyproject.toml with the minimum necessary fixes.

Key fixes you should apply

A) Add missing runtime dependencies (needed now)

  • pyarrow (you are writing parquet in download_prices.py)

  • lxml + html5lib (needed for pandas.read_html() in make universe)

B) Fix setuptools packaging

Your current:

TOML
[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["src"]

will not reliably include subpackages like src.data, src.features, etc. Use setuptools “find” instead.

C) Move “future but not required now” deps into optional extras

This keeps your base environment lighter and more stable, while preserving future stuff.

ChatGPT dijo:

Next step: validate your environment + keys, then freeze the universe snapshot, then start the resumable Alpha Vantage OHLCV download for a small pilot set (so you can debug fast), and only after that scale to the full S&P 500.

Here’s the exact sequence I’d follow.

ChatGPT dijo:

That 403 is coming from Wikipedia blocking requests that don’t send a normal User-Agent. pandas.read_html(url) uses Python’s default urllib user agent, which often gets rejected → HTTP 403 Forbidden.

Fix: fetch the HTML yourself with requests with headers, then pass the HTML string into pandas.read_html().

Replace your src/data/build_universe.py with this version (same CLI, just fixes the download):

Python
# src/data/build_universe.py
import argparse
from datetime import datetime
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import requests

WIKI_SP500_URL = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies"


def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.utcnow().isoformat(timespec="seconds") + "Z"


def fetch_html(url: str, timeout_s: int = 60) -> str:
    headers = {
        # Wikipedia often blocks default urllib user agents
        "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) event-state-forecasting/0.1 (research; contact: you@example.com)",
        "Accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8",
        "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
    }
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout_s)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.text


def fetch_sp500_table() -> pd.DataFrame:
    html = fetch_html(WIKI_SP500_URL)
    tables = pd.read_html(StringIO(html))
    for t in tables:
        cols = [str(c).strip() for c in t.columns.tolist()]
        if "Symbol" in cols and "Security" in cols:
            t = t.copy()
            t.columns = cols
            return t
    raise RuntimeError("Could not find S&P 500 table with columns Symbol and Security")


def build_universe_df() -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = fetch_sp500_table()

    df["Symbol"] = df["Symbol"].astype(str).str.strip()

    keep_cols = [
        "Symbol",
        "Security",
        "GICS Sector",
        "GICS Sub-Industry",
        "Headquarters Location",
        "Date added",
        "CIK",
        "Founded",
    ]
    keep_cols = [c for c in keep_cols if c in df.columns]
    df = df[keep_cols].copy()

    df = df.rename(columns={"Symbol": "ticker", "Security": "security"})
    df["snapshot_utc"] = _utc_now_iso()

    df = df.sort_values("ticker").reset_index(drop=True)
    return df


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--also-latest", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out_path = Path(args.out)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    df = build_universe_df()
    df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)

    if args.also_latest:
        latest_path = Path(args.also_latest)
        latest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        df.to_csv(latest_path, index=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Here’s a simple sanity-check script you can run after make universe to verify everything looks right and to catch common issues (empty file, missing columns, weird ticker formats, duplicates, etc.).

Create: scripts/check_universe.py (or put it in src/cli/ if you prefer—this is standalone).

Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--file",
        default="data/raw/universe/sp500_latest.csv",
        help="Universe CSV to check (default: data/raw/universe/sp500_latest.csv)",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    path = Path(args.file)
    if not path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"[FAIL] File not found: {path}")

    df = pd.read_csv(path)

    print(f"[OK] Loaded: {path}")
    print(f"     Rows: {len(df)} | Cols: {len(df.columns)}")
    print("     Columns:", list(df.columns))

    # Basic required columns
    required = {"ticker"}
    missing = required.difference(df.columns)
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"[FAIL] Missing required columns: {sorted(missing)}")

    # Basic sanity checks
    df["ticker"] = df["ticker"].astype(str).str.strip()

    if df["ticker"].isna().any() or (df["ticker"] == "").any():
        raise SystemExit("[FAIL] Found empty/NaN tickers")

    dup = df["ticker"].duplicated().sum()
    if dup > 0:
        print(f"[WARN] Duplicate tickers found: {dup}")
        print(df[df["ticker"].duplicated(keep=False)].sort_values("ticker").head(20))
    else:
        print("[OK] No duplicate tickers")

    # Expected size check (S&P 500 should be around 500; allow some tolerance)
    if not (450 <= len(df) <= 550):
        print(f"[WARN] Universe size looks unusual for S&P 500: {len(df)} (expected ~500)")

    # Ticker format checks
    tickers = df["ticker"].tolist()
    dots = [t for t in tickers if "." in t]
    dashes = [t for t in tickers if "-" in t]
    spaces = [t for t in tickers if " " in t]

    print(f"[INFO] Tickers with '.': {len(dots)} (examples: {dots[:10]})")
    print(f"[INFO] Tickers with '-': {len(dashes)} (examples: {dashes[:10]})")

    if spaces:
        print(f"[WARN] Tickers with spaces found: {len(spaces)} (examples: {spaces[:10]})")

    # Show head/tail
    print("\n[HEAD]")
    print(df.head(10).to_string(index=False))

    print("\n[TAIL]")
    print(df.tail(10).to_string(index=False))

    # Optional: check snapshot field if present
    if "snapshot_utc" in df.columns:
        unique_snap = df["snapshot_utc"].nunique(dropna=False)
        print(f"\n[INFO] snapshot_utc unique values: {unique_snap}")
        print(f"[INFO] snapshot_utc example: {df['snapshot_utc'].iloc[0]}")

    print("\n[PASS] Universe file looks reasonable.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it from the repo root (venv active):

Good — your pipeline is behaving correctly. The failure is not your code right now: Alpha Vantage is explicitly telling you that TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED is premium for your key, so it returns the “premium endpoint” message and your script stops (correctly) after 1 request.

You can see it in your ledger:

“This is a premium endpoint… subscribe…”

So the next step is to switch to a non-premium endpoint that still gives you daily OHLCV.

What this means for your project

  • You can still build the OHLCV database with Alpha Vantage free tier.

  • You just can’t rely on DAILY_ADJUSTED (and therefore you won’t get split/dividend fields from AV via that endpoint unless you upgrade).

  • You can still compute returns using raw close, and you can later handle splits by other means (or accept that split artifacts exist and document it).

Next step (practical): use TIME_SERIES_DAILY (free) and request outputsize=full

Alpha Vantage’s regular daily time series function is TIME_SERIES_DAILY. It returns daily OHLCV, and supports outputsize=full / compact. (Your code already supports different function names.)

1) Run the pilot again with the free endpoint

Bash
python -m src.data.download_prices \
  --universe data/raw/universe/pilot10.csv \
  --raw-dir data/raw/alphavantage \
  --parsed-dir data/interim/alphavantage_prices \
  --function TIME_SERIES_DAILY \
  --outputsize full \
  --max-requests-per-day 25 \
  --sleep-seconds 15 \
  --force

This should start creating parquets.

Minimal code change required (because your parser currently expects “daily adjusted” fields)

Right now parse_daily_adjusted_json() expects keys like:

  • 5. adjusted close

  • 7. dividend amount

  • 8. split coefficient

TIME_SERIES_DAILY returns only:

  • 1. open, 2. high, 3. low, 4. close, 5. volume

So you must update download_prices.py to parse both schemas depending on the --function.

Patch src/data/download_prices.py (small, safe)

Replace the constant DAILY_KEYS + parse_daily_adjusted_json with this dual-parser approach:

Python
# Replace your DAILY_KEYS with these two:
DAILY_KEYS_DAILY = [
    ("1. open", "open"),
    ("2. high", "high"),
    ("3. low", "low"),
    ("4. close", "close"),
    ("5. volume", "volume"),
]

DAILY_KEYS_DAILY_ADJUSTED = [
    ("1. open", "open"),
    ("2. high", "high"),
    ("3. low", "low"),
    ("4. close", "close"),
    ("5. adjusted close", "adjusted_close"),
    ("6. volume", "volume"),
    ("7. dividend amount", "dividend_amount"),
    ("8. split coefficient", "split_coefficient"),
]


def parse_time_series_json(symbol_used: str, payload: Dict[str, Any], function: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    ts = payload.get("Time Series (Daily)")
    if ts is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing 'Time Series (Daily)' for {symbol_used}. Keys={list(payload.keys())[:10]}")

    if function == "TIME_SERIES_DAILY":
        keys = DAILY_KEYS_DAILY
    elif function == "TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED":
        keys = DAILY_KEYS_DAILY_ADJUSTED
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported function for parsing: {function}")

    rows = []
    for date_str, v in ts.items():
        row: Dict[str, Any] = {"date": pd.to_datetime(date_str), "ticker": symbol_used}
        for k, col in keys:
            if k in v:
                row[col] = float(v[k])
        rows.append(row)

    return pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["ticker", "date"]).reset_index(drop=True)

Then in main(), replace:

Python
df = parse_daily_adjusted_json(sym_used, payload)

with:

Python
df = parse_time_series_json(sym_used, payload, args.function)

And in validate_price_data, remove adjusted_close etc from required columns (you already only require open/high/low/close/volume, so you’re fine).

That’s it.

What about splits/dividends continuity?

Since free TIME_SERIES_DAILY won’t give split events:

  • For now: compute labels using raw close and document that split artifacts exist.

  • Later options:

    1. upgrade Alpha Vantage plan (simplest)

    2. get split/dividend data from another source (not ideal since you wanted AV only)

    3. restrict study window to periods without splits for selected tickers (not great, but possible)

Given your thesis goals (event state / multimodal fusion), it’s academically acceptable to proceed with raw OHLCV as long as you explicitly acknowledge this limitation in threats to validity.

One more small improvement: fix the UTC warning (optional)

Your deprecation warning is harmless, but if you want to clean it:

  • replace datetime.utcnow() with datetime.now(timezone.utc)

Not required right now.

Do this now

  2. Run the pilot with TIME_SERIES_DAILY.

Then we’ll confirm your OHLCV pipeline is solid and start scaling the collector.

ChatGPT dijo:

You’re not hitting a code bug in the parsing logic right now — you’re stopping because Alpha Vantage is returning a Note/Information message, and your is_rate_limited() treats any Note/Information as “rate limited” (which is correct behavior), so the script stops after the first call.

The key thing is: what exactly does the message say? It can mean:

  • “premium endpoint” (like your previous DAILY_ADJUSTED case), or

  • “call frequency exceeded” (per-minute or per-day quota), or

  • another informational error.

Your ledger already contains the exact message; let’s use that and then make your script smarter.

1) First: confirm the exact Alpha Vantage message

Run:

Bash
tail -n 5 data/raw/alphavantage/download_ledger.csv

If the message contains “premium endpoint”, then that function/outputsize combination is not available for your key.

If it contains “call frequency” or “Thank you for using Alpha Vantage” but not “premium endpoint”, then you’re being throttled (per-minute or per-day).

2) Two fixes you should do regardless

A) Update your Makefile default to the free endpoint

Because TIME_SERIES_DAILY_ADJUSTED is clearly premium for your key.

Change your Makefile download_prices target to:

  • --function TIME_SERIES_DAILY

So you don’t accidentally keep calling a premium endpoint later.

B) Remove the dead code path in download_prices.py

You still have parse_daily_adjusted_json() referencing DAILY_KEYS (undefined). It’s not being called now, but it’s a landmine. Delete that whole function.

3) Make the downloader handle different “Note/Information” cases properly

Right now, you treat all Information/Note as “stop for today”. That’s too strict.

We want:

  • premium endpoint → stop (nothing will work today for that function)

  • per-minute throttling → wait and retry the same ticker

  • per-day quota → stop for the day

  • unknown informational → log and stop (safe)

Drop-in patch for src/data/download_prices.py

Make these changes:

(1) Fix the UTC deprecation warning

Replace your _utc_now_iso() with:

Python
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z")

(2) Add helpers to classify messages

Add these near the top (after imports):

Python
def get_notice(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    for k in ("Note", "Information"):
        v = payload.get(k)
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip():
            return v.strip()
    return None

def classify_notice(msg: str) -> str:
    m = msg.lower()
    if "premium endpoint" in m:
        return "premium"
    # Typical throttling language
    if "call frequency" in m or "too many requests" in m or "higher api call frequency" in m:
        if "per day" in m:
            return "rate_limit_day"
        if "per minute" in m or "minute" in m:
            return "rate_limit_minute"
        return "rate_limit"
    return "notice_other"

(3) Change download_one_symbol to return a better error code

Replace this block:

Python
        if is_rate_limited(payload):
